backend: classical expansion of the PR #389 generation (no new generation)

conformance.aspect_note: Deliverable aspect UNCHANGED (720x720 bundle standard). The source canvas was extended vertically (1280 -> 2060 px, +390 px top and bottom) before the standard normalisation, so the subject sits smaller in frame than the #389 normalisation - the swirl now fits instead of running off the top and bottom edges.

expansion.expansion_axis: vertical (top/bottom) at raw scale; horizontal margins come from the clip's own pillarbox normalisation, exactly as in the delivered #389 bundle
expansion.method: Radial continuation + exponential fade (deterministic, per-frame). Diagnosis first: in the DELIVERED 720x720 framing the vortex never approaches the side edges (content x 184..535, minimum side margin 184 px); it runs off the TOP and BOTTOM only, frames 153-192, because the delivered normalisation is the full portrait fit to height. An ellipse-annulus fit was attempted and degenerates on this performance (horizontal semi-axis stable ~170 delivered px, vertical semi-axis -> infinity, residual -> 0): the swirl is a near-vertical spiral column, not a closable ellipse ring, so no ring closure was fabricated. Instead the raw canvas was extended +390 px top and bottom; each band pixel takes the colour sampled where its ray from the vortex centre (304, 640) crosses the old frame edge, exponentially faded to white (tau = 71 raw px). The swirl continues past the old edge and dissolves - smoke behaviour - instead of being guillotined. A 12 px feather strip inside each old edge blends original toward the ray-crossing colour. No randomness and no cross-frame borrowing: frame N's extension is a pure function of frame N, so the bands cannot boil or flicker. The delivered normalisation (fit-height, pillarbox on white) was verified to reproduce the delivered bundle frames at MAD 1.3-2.8 before expansion, and the same normalisation was applied to the expanded canvas.
expansion.ring_phase_frames_delivered: 153-192 (frames touching top/bottom in the delivered bundle)

framing_verification.method: Per-frame content extent (any channel < 235), the same measure that failed both prior candidates, run on the finished normalised 720x720 clip. (The intermediate expanded canvas keeps the raw's native 608 px width, so its left/right extents are the portrait's own; horizontal margins are produced by the pillarbox normalisation exactly as in the delivered bundle - 184 px there, 253 px here because the subject sits smaller.)
framing_verification.seam_verdict: PASS - seam close-ups straddling both old edge lines at peak frames 184 and 160 show no guillotine line and no pattern break: above/below the old edges the swirl's glow continues and feathers into white. Caveat, stated not hidden: the continuation is a RADIAL DISSOLVE (the band texture streaks softly along rays from the vortex centre and fades), not a reconstruction of the arc curvature the generator never drew - it reads as the vortex dissipating into smoke past the old edges. The glyph bands sit fully inside the frame and are untouched.
